pr_body:
When we need to select a qualified provider address based on an implied provider name, we have a special case that the name "terraform" maps to `terraform.io/builtin/terraform`, instead of `registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/terraform` as would be the case for other prefixes.

However, in order for that to work properly we need to use `addrs.ImpliedProviderForUnqualifiedType` instead of `addrs.NewDefaultProvider`, because the latter just unconditionally always produces a "default" provider configuration (belonging to the "hashicorp" namespace on the public registry).

This fixes #25719.

For large Terraform configs, please use a service like Dropbox and share a link to the ZIP file. For security, you can also encrypt the files using our GPG public key.

This can be reproduced by creating a very simple module that outputs the ID of a null resource
```terraform
resource "null_resource" "resource1" {
}

output "null_id" {
  value = null_resource.resource1.id
}
```

applying that, and consuming it as remote data

```terraform
data "terraform_remote_state" "data1" {
  backend = "local"

  config = {
    path = "${path.module}/module1/terraform.tfstate"
  }
}

resource "null_resource" "n1" {
  triggers = {
    id = data.terraform_remote_state.data1.outputs.null_id
  }
}
```
applying this module will get the local state backends ready to reproduce this for reference my test directory looks like
```
.
├── main.tf
├── module1
│   ├── main.tf
│   └── terraform.tfstate
└── terraform.tfstate

1 directory, 4 files
```

By modifying the top `main.tf` to look like
```
resource "null_resource" "n1" {
}
```
we'll no longer be able to plan

### Debug Output

The relevant chunk of the debug output is 
```
2020/07/31 16:02:57 [TRACE] (graphTransformerMulti) Executing graph transform *terraform.MissingProviderTransformer
2020/07/31 16:02:57 [DEBUG] adding implicit provider configuration provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/null"], implied first by null_resource.n1
2020/07/31 16:02:57 [DEBUG] adding implicit provider configuration provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/terraform"], implied first by data.terraform_remote_state.data1
```

comments: Thank you for reporting this! I've reproduced this using the ga version of 0.13.0. For the sake of the next person to touch this, I've put the reproduction case in GitHub to minimize copy-paste work: https://github.com/danieldreier/terraform-issue-reproductions/tree/master/25719

How do i actually fix this locally?

If i understand it correctly, terraform expects its builtin terraform provider to be declared and i can't do that as terraform tells me its removed and builtin.

Thanks for reporting this, @ZymoticB!

During development of Terraform 0.13 we introduced a special case to make the name `terraform` implicitly to `terraform.io/builtin/terraform` rather than the default of `registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/terraform`, because the latter is a legacy provider intended for Terraform 0.11 users and isn't Terraform 0.13 compatible. However, it seems like we missed updating one place to honor that special case, so it was using the default source address prefix exclusively, even for `terraform`.

I proposed a fix for this over in #25948.

To work around this in the meantime, I think it would work to explicitly remove the remnant resource from the state. In the reproduction case, that would be a command like the following:

```
terraform state rm data.terraform_remote_state.data1
```

With the resource removed from both the configuration and the state, Terraform should no longer feel the need to find a provider configuration for it.

review_comments:
As you can see with the other APIs in this package, we typically have methods to represent the relationships between the different address types, which initially serve as a sort of executable documentation for what relationships are meaningful. In other words, this method represents the statement `Module + Resource => ConfigResource`, similar to how `Absolute` represents `ModuleInstance + Resource => AbsResource`. The `addrs` package as a whole exists to explicitly represent all of Terraform's address types and their relationships in a strongly-typed way, so this is a logical extension of that mission.

This `ConfigResource` type was recently added as part of 0.13 work, so it's not yet used as prolifically as `AbsResource` and `AbsResourceInstance`, but will grow increasingly important now that it's the primary representation of a resource that hasn't yet had its `count` and `for_each` expressions evaluated.
